Tagtreevivor S7: Open Season - 3rd-volume-confessional

Tagtreevivor S7: Open Season
confessionals / 3rd-volume-confessional
Pilot 2/11/2026 5:54 PM
5:54 PM
Congratulations on being cast on Tagtreevivor Season 7! You have about 4 days trapped in here with production until the season starts. Until then... 1. Tell us what you've been up to since you last played! 2. Give a prediction of the cast or what you're expecting for the season! 3. How will this game be different than the previous Tagtreevivor game you played? 4. What's your star sign?
3rd - Volume 2/12/2026 1:37 PM
We are so back
1:38 PM
I will answer all these questions later today
3rd - Volume 2/12/2026 6:14 PM
1. I played Tagtree Season 4: Nicoleverse in May 2025. I am now 25. That's different. I also live alone in a new place as my roommate moved in with his girlfriend closer to his work. I say roommate because in my head that's a close relationship but a lot of people have random fuckers as roommate. My roommate is my best friend I've know for 15+ years. I am 25. As for what I am doing, I mean I'm still in a choir and I'm still doing improv but there were breaks in the last 8 months. I joined a run club but now its winter. I read 50 books last year but didn't finish any in January. I have a more clear goal on my novels and writing trajectory but I haven't really implemented them, with some minor revising occurring on my main one. I did go to Dragonsteel Nexus which is author Brandon Sanderson's convention and is basically a fantasy book convention, where I got to go to panels composed of a lot of different authors in different phases of their career and that really motivated me. Mainly stalled since due to holidays and being sick a lot of January. Also a lot of my writing brain goes into confessional for ORGs which brings me too: ORGs! Which I haven't done a ton of. I was prod for just edgic on Season 28 but I had to drop midseason as prod cause I had to deal with moving (I thought I'd be able to live alone in same complex but the prices went up too high so I had to look around more aggressively - kinda stressful and also during hottest part of the year). Doormatt asked me to do Snack 10 with him for the Blood vs Water season. We flopped kinda, going out back to back right before merge. It was a weird time for me cause I just got very busy with work, I was having a rough month and I had medication changes (unrelated to rough month). So I was trying a KHam esque strategy to just be good at comps and kinda dip. I am not KHam, that man is a legend. Also the vote I got voted out on I realized if I made merge I'd be travelling during the beginning so i was in a mixed spot. (edited)
6:15 PM
(welcome back to Volume confs where I use the character limit to respond to questions)
6:16 PM
So yeah that was a weird season, lot of background stuff that was not ideal for me, but I did kind of ok all things considered. Blood vs Water is cursed though
6:21 PM
Took a break from ORGs, got the soft invite for this season so planned for it but wasn't sure if I'd make it depeneding on criteria of the season. I had an opportunity to play Survivor Rewind: Pearl Islands which was their last season before All Stars - they essentially recreate the experience which was really cool. 3 day cycles with reward that mattered for a cool survival task system which impacted challenge performance. (Mainly losing tiebreakers). But great time, 3 day cycles are cool. That started January 1st, and tragically I am too good at survivor so I made it to February 7th, day 37 where I was voted at f4. Thing is, we flipped the game on f10 for a rock draw to try to get "tribal majority" (5-4-1 split, where the 1 was an outcast from the og 5 tribe and I was in the 4, but the 1 voted with us). We lost it but I didn't get rocked out and then we got pagonged except for me and the outcast who found our way to f4, he got 2nd. I was hero of the season. I guess I have hero energy but mainly I was playing from the bottom the whole time and might've had a shot to win had I setup and played f4 better.

I do want to mention one thing I did really like about Rewind, which was there tribal council question system, and as someone who attended a lot of tribal councils (4 in premerge, f10-f4 in merge) I experienced it a lot. Prod would @ each individual player with a question designed for them as tribal council chat opened up and you had to respond to the question with a real sounding answer (basically don't give one word answers) or you lost your vote. It was much more engaging than the tribals I've had here or elsewhere in the smORGon sphere where its just @ing who is online 20 minutes before tribal. Also sometimes it would be a general question to everyone or popcorn (or both), popcorn being where prod asks one player a question and they ask another player until every player has answered a question and the last player to be asked gets to pick someone to ask another question to.

3rd - Volume 3/26/2026 10:31 AM
My game is based on the quote “Be like water” I went with the flow, I adapted. I was never the target, I never had to steer. It was going my way. Then I got my chance at f8, picking up Typo’s idol and coasting into f5 from there. There was a Sunleaf 4 plan, but that got blown up. So I adapted. At f6 I learned a move was being made without me, and this is where I shaped the game. It became less about strategy and more about the endgame I wanted to see. I built real relationships with people and I honored them. I organized the snipe on Guyguard. I gave immunity to Gersh, if it was needed and still idoled myself. Then despite losing f5 immunity by 4 seconds, I still was the deciding vote. I went with the people I spent hours with in VC in tweak sessions before votes. I did not go with the person who tried to blindside me the whole merge. And I think I was proved right, as she was nasty. That’s not someone I want winning. You may think I did nothing, but I bided my time and chose my end game. I collected late game masks, and I kept them to myself. And because I made a pact at f5, I got the information I needed to secure the FTC I wanted. In survivor you don’t get to force what you want, there are repercussions. You have to adapt to what the group wants and redirect the energy a way from you. I let other people take the spotlight while still getting all necessary information on the vote. Gersh’s game and my game work in tandem. Without me, he can’t do what he did, without him I can’t either. I never burned any bridges until the end. I was genuine with who I am with all of you in the jury. I enjoyed talking to all of you, and my game has been making friends with all of you, while still getting my way in the game. This is what I played for. I didn’t control every vote, but I controlled my position in every vote. By maintaining good relations with everyone in the game. I was like water, flowing through the game. But I directed the water in the end. My choices. This game

3rd - Volume 3/27/2026 12:47 PM
Looking back on my first FTC, I got roasted a lot for being under the radar and low visibility. I feel the same will happen here. The difference is that I drove end game this time and I won important immunities. Is it enough though? My case right now is that I played an under the radar game as going into merge I thought I might be a threat due to my past season. I was positioned well after every vote and had neutral to positive connections with every player for most of the game. I had the connections I needed to get the information I needed and I avoided votes by getting an idol at the right time and being difficult to target. Then I chose the end game f6-f4 and got my biggest adversary to give me immunity just by seeming amenable. Which was my whole game. I found a very safe path to FTC and you could argue I could’ve tried weaker players but they were not necessarily aligned with me and their leader tried to undermine me every vote in which I countered. You can argue hypotheticals, but my choices got me to the end.
12:48 PM
Fuck it’s hard to be succinct
12:51 PM
I felt I would come in as a threat due to my past game, so I purposely played an under the radar game in a threats alliance. Despite that not working out, I had the connections I needed to stay informed and not be a target. My connections gave me a crucial idol valid from f8-f6. I won crucial immunities to choose my path and even though I was being undermined I countered every move, and I made the decisions that led to f6-f4 boots. Didn’t have to help Gersh or Cake at f6 with the info Hi gave me, didn’t have to boot Hi at f5, could’ve chosen Gersh. I could’ve given fire to Venus at f4. I did not. These were my moves and they got me to the end with people I respect, and who played different games than me in which I believe mine stands out
